targets.title: Automatization in second language acquisition: What does the coefﬁcient of variation tell us?
targets.evidence_quote:
The study was a partial conceptual replication of Hulstijn

et al. (2009), using the same analyses on a subset of the same speeded tasks.
targets.outcome_quote:
The general ﬁnding was that RTs, standard deviations, and CVs all decreased as a

function of participants’ English proﬁciency level: from intermediate ESL learners

(L1 Korean), to advanced ESL learners, to native English speakers. This ﬁnding

was in stark contrast to Hulstijn et al.’s (2009) study, who failed to ﬁnd a decrease
in Dutch high school students’ CV over three consecutive grade years, in which

the students received ESL instruction in school and plentiful exposure to English

(e.g., through the media) outside the classroom.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central sentence-processing CV finding decreases with proficiency, explicitly in stark contrast to the original null result. Supporting the theoretical automatization hypothesis is disagreement with the target original finding.

reasoning: New Korean-background English learners and native English speakers conceptually replicate Hulstijn et al. Experiment 1; the central result contradicts the original null CV change.
